deepdive.sec: Diversified Financial Services — Investment Banking / Capital Markets, Private Credit (incl. ARC/distressed), Wealth & Asset Management, Affordable Home Loans

bull_bear.body: Dividend policy: 50% of Private Markets PAT distributed annually; ₹570 cr aggregate dividend paid/proposed over trailing 4 quarters (~₹5.95/share). Freed-up capital from Private Markets book de-risking is being redirected first to Wealth & Asset Management, then Affordable Home Loans; CACM and Private Markets are self-funding and require no fresh capital. No demerger/listing of individual businesses in the near term, despite investor prompting (peer comparisons of listed broking + wealth-management spin-offs) — management wants scale first.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- FPI ownership in Indian equities down to ~15% from a high of ~19% — a swing factor for CACM/Private-Markets deal conversion timing.
- Geopolitical/oil-price overhang (West Asia crisis, oil ~$90-100) cited as a driver of the FPI-selling episode and IPO-market pause through Q4FY26/Q1FY27.
- Real-estate lending: management explicitly staying cautious/slow ("risk-adjusted returns... not attractive enough"), flags the up-cycle in real estate sales as over — a read-through risk for real-estate-linked private credit peers too.
- Wealth Management ROE still subdued (~12%) after 3 years of talent/infrastructure investment — productivity ramp is unproven until it shows in FY27 numbers.
- Asset Management still loss-making (~₹30 cr FY26), multi-year runway to profitability.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident/promotional tone throughout, with explicit multi-year framing ("model CACM/Private Markets peak-to-peak") to pre-empt quarter-to-quarter volatility concerns. Management proactively disclosed one-off items (tax-refund interest, Labour Code impact) and gave granular segment/AUM/loan-book breakdowns (e.g., full Private Markets book composition on request) rather than deflecting. Fielded a pointed analyst question on CACM employee-cost-vs-revenue math directly rather than avoiding it.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Bajaj Allianz's June-2025 purchase of 2.1% of JM Financial Home Loans at ₹48/share implies a ₹3,100 cr valuation for the Affordable Home Loans subsidiary alone — an external, market-set data point for sum-of-the-parts investors.
- Management explicitly separates "loan book" optics from revenue: interest income has de-grown for two years purely due to deliberate real-estate book runoff, which depresses consolidated revenue even as every operating segment grows — a case where headline consol. revenue is a poor proxy for underlying momentum.
- Real estate lending will stop being reported as a standalone bucket going forward — it will be folded into the overall standard/corporate loan book (management will still disclose the real-estate % of total), signaling declining strategic emphasis on that vertical as a distinct business line.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Increased payout to shareholders (1.6x increase over last two years); Aggregate payout of Rs. 5.95 per share over last 5 quarters".
- Group balance sheet: Net Worth Rs. 10,899 Cr and Capital Employed Rs. 11,197 Cr at June 30, 2026 (Rs. 10,605 Cr / Rs. 10,898 Cr at March 31, 2026); Gross D/E 1.0x versus 1.1x, with borrowings down to Rs. 10,882 Cr from Rs. 11,522 Cr; BVPS Rs. 113.9.
- Private Markets segment deleveraging: Gross D/E 1.9x (FY24) to 1.1x (FY25) to 0.9x (FY26) to 0.8x (Q1FY27), with borrowing down from Rs. 12,741 Cr to Rs. 5,766 Cr and total assets from Rs. 19,350 Cr to Rs. 12,879 Cr over the same span.
- Affordable Home Loans has been funded by parent equity infusions of Rs. 108 Cr (FY22), Rs. 100 Cr (FY23), Rs. 25 Cr (FY24) and Rs. 225 Cr (FY25), with Nil in FY26; segment Gross D/E 2.3x in FY26.
- Capital is deployed across segments with disclosed capital employed at Q1FY27: Private Markets Rs. 6,814 Cr, Treasury and others Rs. 1,389 Cr, Wealth Management Rs. 1,179 Cr, Corporate Advisory Rs. 861 Cr, Home Loans Rs. 851 Cr and Asset Management Rs. 103 Cr.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **CACM** (IB + institutional equities): FY26 net revenue ₹789 cr (+11% YoY), opex-adjusted PAT ₹347 cr, capital employed ₹829 cr → ROE ~47%. Q4FY26 segment PAT only ₹39 cr — hit by the primary-issuance drought. Research coverage expanded to ~400 stocks active + ~150 soft coverage, cited as the largest on the Street; new derivatives desk added to institutional equities last year.
- **Private Markets**: FY26 operating PBT +3.5x to ₹742 cr, PAT (post-minority) +3.6x to ₹543 cr on capital employed ~₹6,600 cr; Q4FY26 segment PAT (post-minority) ₹78 cr. Loan book down from ₹10,000 cr (FY24) → ₹5,000 cr (FY25) → ₹4,000 cr (FY26), driven by real-estate repayments/prepayments; management now pivoting to a fee-based, syndication-led model rather than growing an on-balance-sheet lending book (self-capped debt:equity of 2:1–3:1).
- **Wealth Management**: FY26 net revenue ₹775 cr (+9% YoY), PAT ₹132 cr, capital employed ₹1,157 cr → ROE ~12%; Q4FY26 segment PAT ₹39 cr (hit by market volatility). RM/sales headcount +30% YoY to 1,046; branches +10 to 72; franchisees to 874. Recurring AUM ~₹31,000 cr (+10% YoY, 29% of total); overall Wealth AUM >₹1,00,000 cr. Revenue split ~50% recurring (fees/commission/interest) vs ~50% transactional (broking + other); broking-only ROE 25-30% given smaller capital base; margin trade finance book grew from ₹300-400 cr to ~₹2,000 cr.
- **Asset Management**: FY26 revenue +38% YoY; MF management fees +65% to ~₹44 cr; segment loss (post-minority) ~₹30 cr for FY26, Q4FY26 loss ₹5 cr — still in an investment/scaling phase (management flags AM has the highest operating leverage once profitable, ~2-year runway to breakeven). Non-liquid MF average AUM ~₹10,500 cr; AM headcount +17% YoY to 217.
- **Affordable Home Loans**: FY26 revenue +25% YoY to ₹455 cr; PAT (post-minority) +45% to ₹74 cr; capital employed ~₹833 cr; Q4FY26 segment PAT ₹25 cr. AUM +22% YoY to ~₹3,460-3,500 cr; branch network 151; customer base >33,000; gross NPA 0.5%, collection efficiency 99.4%.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Corporate Advisory and Capital Markets (Investment Banking, Institutional Equities) is described as having "Leadership; Best in class relationships", "Strong sticky repeat business" and "Highest ever client addition", supported by a filed IPO pipeline of ~Rs. 1,50,000 crore across 60 transactions (excluding filed IPO transactions of Jio Platforms Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited; IPOs yet to be filed would be additional).
- Private Markets is framed as "Bespoke solutions and access to private capital for clients" with "capital, connectivity, innovation and solutions led expertise" and a "Syndication/co-invest" approach to improve risk adjusted returns.
- Wealth and Asset Management (manufacturing, distribution, advisory) is described as a "Unique Platform" with a "Strong multi-decadal growth opportunity" and expansion into manufacturing products.
- Affordable Home Loans is positioned as a "Pure-play HFC with no Developer Loan" in the affordable segment, with a granular book at an average ticket size of ~Rs. 10 lakhs.
- The deck describes the mix as having "Differentiated and counter cyclical elements to the business" and the group as "Fully capitalized".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group structure] Effective ownership at June 30, 2026: JM Financial Credit Solutions, Institutional Securities, Services, Properties and Holdings, CR Retail Malls and Overseas Entities at 100.0%; JM Financial Products 99.8%; JM Financial Home Loans 96.5%; JM Financial Asset Reconstruction Company 81.8%; JM Financial Asset Management 59.5%; JM Financial Trustee Company 25.0%.
- [Accounting adjustments] FY26 comparatives are restated by the company for receipt of interest on income tax refund of Rs. 113 crore and the statutory impact of new labour codes of ~Rs. 22 crore (net Rs. 91 crore pre-tax and NCI; Rs. 69 crore post tax and NCI), so FY26 appears on both adjusted and reported bases in the deck.
- [Minority interests] Non-controlling interests are material and concentrated: NCI is "primarily on account of JM Financial Asset Reconstruction Company Limited", with group NCI of Rs. 298 Cr and a separate share of Security Receipt holders (Rs. 299 Cr in Private Markets at Q1FY27 versus Rs. 408 Cr in FY26).
- [Asset quality] Affordable Home Loans GNPA/NNPA improved to 0.75%/0.50% from 1.5%/1.0% in Q1FY26; Private Markets Net NPA stands at Rs. 130 Cr, unchanged from FY26 and down from Rs. 279 Cr in FY24.
- [Asset Management drag] Asset Management is the one loss-making platform in the deck, with negative operating profit in FY24, FY25, FY26 and both quarters shown, alongside falling MF AAUM and SIP book.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: CACM employee cost rose ₹165 cr → ₹265 cr (FY24→FY26, +₹100 cr) against a ₹259 cr revenue increase over the same period and a ~₹100 cr PAT increase — management frames this as deliberate front-loading of hiring (incl. new derivatives desk, expanded research) ahead of a pipeline that grew from ~₹40,000-50,000 cr to ~₹1,40,000 cr. Digital investment (BlinkX) of ₹40-50 cr/year is being "cut down significantly" over the next 3-6 months, expected to show savings from Q1FY27 itself. Wealth Management margin expansion is the explicit FY27 focus as newly-hired RM productivity ramps.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** First note in this store for JMFINANCIL/523405. FY26 full-year: consol. PAT ₹1,202 cr (+46% YoY, +38% adj. ex one-offs); every "grow" segment (CACM, Wealth, Asset Mgmt, Affordable Home Loans) posted double-digit-to-high revenue growth; Private Markets loan book shrank to ₹4,000 cr (from ₹10,000 cr in FY24) on planned de-risking; Q4/Q1FY27 CACM hit by an FPI-selling-driven primary-market freeze.
- **Q1 FY27 → check:** Did the "mid-April revival" in deal activity sustain? Any concrete pipeline conversion (IPOs/QIPs/blocks) materializing? BlinkX digital-broking cost cuts showing up in Wealth Management segment P&L? Private Markets standard loan book progressing toward the ₹5,000 cr March-2027 target? Any update on the AIF pre-IPO/PE fund first closes (>₹1,000 cr targeted each)?
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- Private Markets recovery: reiterated ₹250-300 cr/year target for FY26/27/28 — FY26 delivered >₹270 cr, "pretty much on target" for FY27.
- Private Markets standard loan book: grow 15-20% YoY — target ~₹5,000 cr by March 2027 (from ~₹4,000 cr); distressed credit (₹3,665 cr) to grow ~15%; equity+alternatives capped at ≤20% of total ~₹13,000 cr book.
- Target segment return assumptions given: standard loans 13-14%, distressed credit 16-18%, equity/alternatives 15-16%.
- Wealth Management: net inflows targeted at ~20% AUM growth (~₹6,000 cr) for FY27, excluding mark-to-market; standalone (ex-broking) business targeted to break even in FY27, with digital (BlinkX) cost base to be "cut down significantly" over the next 3-6 months.
- Group-level long-term target: 15% revenue growth and 15% ROE (mgmt: "we are kind of there" on an investment-cycle-adjusted basis).
- Affordable Home Loans: IPO targeted by 2028-29; AUM to keep growing ~25% YoY.
- CACM: no explicit revenue guidance — management asks investors to model this segment "peak-to-peak" (targets doubling the business every 4-5 years) given quarter-to-quarter volatility from deal-timing.
- No demerger/listing of individual segments planned in the near term ("maybe after a year or 2 years").
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: CACM pipeline ~₹1,40,000 cr of filed IPOs (55 filings) plus a growing non-IPO pipeline (QIPs, blocks, M&A, PE placements); management expects this to nearly double YoY (June-Sept 2025 base vs June-Oct 2026) to ~₹2,00,000 cr. FPI selling (~4-5 months) has stalled conversion — deal activity was near-zero in March-April 2026, with a mid-April revival; management expects H2 FY27 to be materially stronger as a ~6-month lag typically drives corporates from equity issuance toward credit/PE placements when equity markets stay shut. Asset Management: first performing-credit AIF (~₹347 cr committed) is one deal from full deployment; second performing-credit fund ("Select Credit") and a pre-IPO fund are in roadshow, pre-IPO fund near first close (total raise target >₹1,000 cr), to be followed by a PE fund targeting a similar raise.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Cross-segment "flywheel": IB transaction clients feed Wealth Management account openings (transactional revenue), which convert to recurring AUM over time; Wealth referrals into the investment bank are also rising ("reverse origination"). Asset Management AIF platform (performing credit, Select Credit, pre-IPO, upcoming PE fund) is a multi-year optionality layer once each fund scales past its investment phase.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Two years into its strategic pivot (announced May 2024), JM Financial has delivered broad-based revenue/profit growth across all four "grow" segments (CACM +26% 2-yr revenue, Wealth +17%, Asset Mgmt +38%, Affordable Home Loans +37%) while deliberately de-risking/shrinking the legacy Private Markets balance sheet (loan book down from ₹10,000 cr in FY24 to ₹4,000 cr in FY26). Q4/Q1 FY27 near-term optics are muddied by an FPI-selling-driven capital-markets slowdown (near-zero deal activity in March-April, reviving mid-April), but management expects a much stronger H2 FY27 as the IPO/QIP/block pipeline (~₹1,40,000 cr filed, seen doubling to ~₹2,00,000 cr by October) converts once volatility eases.
